newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent sheds gains as Iraq steps back.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent sheds gains as Iraq steps back.

text.p: IPE November Brent futures shed the day's gains to close five cents lower on Friday after the market interpreted Iraq's retraction of a threat to fire at U.S. and allied patrol planes as a signal to sell.

November Brent, which took over from October as the prompt month on Friday night, closed at $23.12 a barrel having earlier scrambled to a high of $23.52 a barrel. It dipped to $22.66 a barrel before panic selling eased just before the close.
A thinly-traded October contract closed up 26 cents at $24.13 a barrel.

Floor traders said some sellers had second thoughts and decided not to risk going short over the weekend in view of the U.S. buildup in the Gulf and the chance of an air strike against Iraq despite an official statement from Baghdad that Iraqi missiles would not be fired on U.S. and allied patrol planes overflying Iraq.
"The news that came out indicated there would not be any action so the market dumped...it became very panicky and those who were long had to get out," a floor trader said.
"People are very nervous. This has nothing to do with oil and people are worried about what might happen over the weekend and some chose to go home long," he added.
IPE gas oil futures, which closed before the news from Iraq appeared, settled $2.25 a tonne higher on what brokers said was good fundamental demand for heating oil in Europe and the United States.
Oct gas oil settled at $221.75 a tonne, gaining strength late in the session after NYMEX heating oil broke through psychological resistance of 70 cents a gallon.
